1.title: Consistently Below Expectations
1.summary: Performance regularly falls below the essential requirements of the role and needs immediate, structured support.

useWhen.1: Key responsibilities are repeatedly missed or delivered below the agreed standard.
useWhen.2: Performance gaps continue even after expectations, guidance and support have been provided.
useWhen.3: The impact is material enough to require a clear improvement plan and close follow-up.

evidence.1: Repeated missed deadlines or incomplete work
evidence.2: Frequent quality, conduct or reliability concerns
evidence.3: Documented coaching with little or no sustained improvement

1.reminder: Use evidence from the full review period. A single difficult incident should not, by itself, determine the rating.

2.title: Below Expectations
2.summary: Some responsibilities are being met, but performance is inconsistent and still falls short in important areas.

useWhen.1: The employee delivers part of the role successfully but needs regular prompting or correction.
useWhen.2: Results, behaviour or reliability are inconsistent across the appraisal period.
useWhen.3: Improvement is visible, but the employee has not yet reached the expected standard.

evidence.3: Progress against an agreed development plan, with gaps still remaining

2.reminder: Be specific about the gaps and identify the support, coaching or resources required for improvement.

3.title: Meets Expectations
3.summary: Performance is dependable and consistently meets the normal requirements of the role.

useWhen.1: Core responsibilities are completed to the expected quality and within reasonable timelines.
useWhen.2: The employee demonstrates the knowledge, conduct and reliability required for the position.
useWhen.3: Performance is steady, professional and aligned with agreed objectives.

evidence.3: Positive contribution to team and organisational goals

3.reminder: A rating of 3 is a positive and credible result. It represents solid, fully acceptable performance.

4.title: Exceeds Expectations
4.summary: Performance is frequently above the normal requirements of the role and creates clear additional value.

useWhen.1: The employee regularly delivers stronger quality, speed, ownership or initiative than expected.
useWhen.2: They solve problems proactively and contribute beyond their basic responsibilities.
useWhen.3: Their performance has a visible positive impact on colleagues, clients or business outcomes.

evidence.1: Consistently strong results beyond agreed targets
evidence.3: Positive feedback supported by measurable outcomes

4.reminder: Explain what was above expectation and how it created value. Avoid using this rating only as a reward for effort.

5.title: Consistently Exceeds Expectations
5.summary: Performance is exceptional, sustained and clearly distinguished from the normal expectations of the role.

useWhen.1: Outstanding results were delivered consistently across the review period, not only on isolated tasks.
useWhen.2: The employee created significant measurable value or demonstrated exceptional leadership and impact.
useWhen.3: The evidence clearly supports performance at the highest level of the scale.

evidence.1: Exceptional and sustained delivery against major objectives
evidence.2: Significant business, client, safety, quality or team impact
evidence.3: Clear examples that distinguish the performance from a strong rating of 4

5.reminder: Reserve 5 for rare, well-supported performance. It should be backed by clear examples and measurable impact.

pdf.recommendedDescription: These recommendations are mandatory supervisor inputs and form part of the submitted appraisal record.
pdf.acknowledgementDescription: The employee is notified immediately after submission and may acknowledge the appraisal and provide feedback.
pdf.formulaNote: Final score = sum of each section rating multiplied by the section weight assigned to this employee for the appraisal cycle.
